newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Portugal Aug inflation seen 0.1-0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Portugal Aug inflation seen 0.1-0.3 pct.

text.p: Portugal's consumer price inflation for August is expected to be between 0.1 and 0.3 percent, compared with 0.2 percent in July, helped by the impact of a reduction in Value Added Tax (VAT), analysts said.

"I'd like to believe that we will begin to feel some impact from the fall in VAT, but it will be very marginal, with prices going up 0.1 percent," said Nuno Botelho of Banco Mello de Investimentos, one of seven analysts polled by Reuters.
VAT in some goods and services, including dairy products, fell to 12 percent from 17 percent in Portugal in July.
If August inflation stands at 0.1-0.3 percent, year-on-year inflation will fall to 3.4-3.6 percent and average inflation to 3.3 percent.

In July, average inflation was 3.4 percent and year-on-year inflation was 3.8 percent. In August 1995 the monthly increase was 0.5 percent, year-on-year inflation was 4.0 percent and average inflation was 4.3 percent.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) is expected to release August inflation data by September 13.
"The reduction in VAT in July had no impact on July figures, and we consider it will have only a small impact in August," said Pedro Braz Teixeira of Banco Santander de Negocios (BSN).

Braz Teixeira, who forecast an August price rise of 0.3 percent, said: "In August 1995 inflation was very much penalised by the behaviour of poultry prices, which represented 0.4 percent of the monthly increase of 0.5 percent.
"In August this year, there was a significant seasonal increase in poultry prices, but not as big as last year."
Luis Santos of Banco Totta & Acores, forecasting a 0.2 percent increase in August prices, expected a weakening in price pressures on beef products due to the "mad cow" scare.
